source_claims.statement: Redirect to /concerto/. Found SOAP endpoint. Basic XXE produced 500s. Analyzed WSDL. Tried CDATA, error-based, OOB with Interactsh, external DTD hosting. Combined external DTD + error-based to exfiltrate.
CDATA failed because entities not processed. Pure error-based did not give clean content. Cramming all logic into one request failed. Multiple endpoints under /concerto/services vulnerable.

research_questions.formulation: After basic XXE and CDATA fail, can an external DTD combined with error-based techniques produce usable file content from the SOAP endpoints?
research_questions.anchor: combination of external DTD hosting with error-based after earlier methods failed
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether entity processing can be leveraged for exfiltration
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that 500 errors or CDATA failure mean XXE is unusable

environment_model_updates: External entities processed; error messages can leak system-id

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: endpoint exploration, WSDL analysis, testing standard XXE variants
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: splitting attack between hosted DTD and main request after in-band methods failed

negative_inconclusive: Pure error-based: no clean file content
unobserved_history: exact DTD content and error payloads used
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat early 500s or CDATA failure as falsification of XXE
Success required composition of external DTD + error-based
next_evidence_actions: Note fix by disabling DTD processing
layer_b_candidate_principles: When standard XXE techniques fail, composing external DTD hosting with error-based or OOB methods can still yield exfiltration
Error messages that leak system-id or file paths are positive signals even if content is not clean
model_vs_harness: Choosing to host an external DTD and split the attack is model reasoning; systematic SOAP/WSDL testing and OOB confirmation can be harness.
